unsupported_claims: The largest graph was the Twitter network with roughly 10 million nodes (about 10.3 million)
The Twitter network had on the order of a billion edges (about 1.5-1.7 billion)
Attributing the Twitter network as the largest benchmark graph used in LINE's experiments
rationale: The evidence does not report the size of the specific largest benchmark graph used to evaluate LINE; the Twitter figures (175 million users, around twenty billion edges) come from a general statement about 2012 networks, not from LINE's experiments, and the answer's node count (~10 million) and edge count (~1.5-1.7 billion) are invented and contradict the cited Twitter figures. The correct response would have been to say the papers do not report this specific size.
